pr_title: drivers: flash: stm32g4: Flush caches after erase and write
pr_body:
Flush the caches after erasing.
This commit fixes sporadic kernel panics when writing big data chunks
to the flash. (data bus errors)

Fixes #32221
pr_comments:
> The Reference Manual stands:
> 
> > If an erase operation in Flash memory also concerns data in the data or instruction cache,
> > you have to make sure that these data are rewritten before they are accessed during code
> > execution. If this cannot be done safely, it is recommended to flush the caches by setting the
> > DCRST and ICRST bits in the Flash access control register (FLASH_ACR).
> 
> Therefore I would flush cashes only prior the erase operation.
> 
> This is just comment as I'm not part of STM team here.

I think it doesn't matter because it is not standard cache but an ART accelerator (Adaptive real-time memory accelerator).
As soon as there is a write operation both flash and cache are updated. So there is no need for a real flush but rather a cache invalidation. This is what is done. And so we should probably spoke about cache invalidate instead of flush ... but this is the word used in Reference Manual.

issue_context.title: Sporadic kernel panics on stm32g4 flash erase/writes
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When writing big data chunks to the flash of an STM32G4 SoC, sporadic kernel panics occur.
It seems that a cache flush is needed after each erase. 

**To Reproduce**
Build mcuboot for the nucleo_g474re and update several times.
Sometimes you will see a panic.

**Expected behavior**
Flash write and erase should work without panic

**Impact**
Firmware updates on stm32g4 series do not work

**Logs and console output**
````
E: ***** BUS FAULT *****
E:   Precise data bus error
E:   BFAR Address: 0xfab1f1a4
E: r0/a1:  0x0000045d  r1/a2:  0x00000000  r2/a3:  0xfab1f1a4
E: r3/a4:  0x20000208 r12/ip:  0xa0000000 r14/lr:  0x080043e1
E:  xpsr:  0x6100000f
E: Faulting instruction address (r15/pc): 0x08003d6a
E: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 0: CPU exception on CPU 0
E: Fault during interrupt handling
E: Current thread: 0x20000208 (unknown)
E: Halting system
````
comments: why low @erwango? this affects all stm32g4 users that use the flash driver.

@alexanderwachter This is from zephyr point of view: one series, one driver, not a regression (from what I saw) and not systematic. But doesn't prevent to review quickly and push so that it's getting merged.

review_comments:
According to STM32G4 Reference Manual, and I found that:
Chapter 3.3.7

> **Programming and caches**
> If a Flash memory write access concerns some data in the data cache, the Flash write
> access modifies the data in the Flash memory and the data in the cache.
> If an erase operation in Flash memory also concerns data in the data or instruction cache,
> you have to make sure that these data are rewritten before they are accessed during code
> execution. If this cannot be done safely, it is recommended to flush the caches

So flush is necessary for erase operation only.
> Therefore I would flush cashes only prior the erase operation.
